nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 3b Handoff
nodes.rationale: Ten tasks, seventeen commits. Closes ROADMAP.md's Phase 1 mesh-format line — STL, OBJ and 3MF all ingest to the same thumbnail and the same three rungs, and no migration was needed, which is the evidence slice 3's seam was cut in the right place.

nodes.label: Caps::max_triangles
nodes.rationale: MAX_DEPTH bounds recursion depth; nothing bounded breadth, and the work is branching^depth. A 604-byte package emitted 16,777,216 triangles at roughly a million times amplification — a sub-kilobyte file would kill a worker limited to 2 GiB, worse than refusing it because the process dies, the lease drops, and the retry feeds the same file back in. Checked as triangles accumulate. Refusing at the budget means doing the work up to it: 7.7 s at 278 MB peak RSS, recorded as a known ceiling.

nodes.label: quick-xml Security Floor
nodes.rationale: quick-xml 0.37 carried RUSTSEC-2026-0194 (quadratic-time parse) and RUSTSEC-2026-0195 (unbounded namespace-declaration allocation). Both sit in the one component that reads attacker-controlled XML, so they would have hollowed out the caps the slice exists to provide. Pinned at 0.41 and recorded in the spec as a security floor with the RUSTSEC ids.

nodes.label: Whole-Branch Adversarial Review
nodes.rationale: Every task passed its own review with spec compliance clean, and the whole-branch review then found a Critical. Per-task reviews could not see it: each was asked 'does this code match its brief?', and it did — the defect was in the plan. Only a reviewer looking at the whole path with permission to be adversarial had the standing to find it.

nodes.label: Tests That Could Not Fail
nodes.rationale: Five tests passed for the wrong reason, all authored in the plan rather than the implementations: std::io::repeat's specialised read_to_end made the naive implementation error too; unpinned transform and composition ordering; a zip-bomb fixture with no _rels/.rels that never reached the cap it was named for. Each fix was the same shape — assert the specific number or the specific message, never merely that an error occurred. A bare expect_err is how this keeps happening.

nodes.label: Per-Service Resource Ceilings
nodes.rationale: deploy.resources.limits added mid-slice at the owner's request: worker 2.0 cores and 2 GiB, and concurrency halved to 2. Throughput fell from 89.4 to 42.8 files/s while peak memory stayed at 2% of the ceiling, so the trade was CPU for fit — the stack now runs on a machine without gigabytes to spare, and raising LAPIDARY_WORKER_CONCURRENCY recovers throughput where there is room. Verified as actually applied via docker inspect, not merely declared.
